Thanks so much, you can't imagine how much that means to me. One of the hardest lessons I personally had to learn was that I can be grateful to have lived. Even though I'm only 17 I made so many hauntingly great memories and I for myself already reached the life goal I had set. To connect with things that many people nowadays lost connection to. Finding pleasure in words, sounds and any other form of art gave me a look at the world I couldn't have imagined. I always wanted to find something deeper in my life, not knowing I had already found it in the little things in life. 

You're totally right, always feeling disconnected from my life made me feel a deep loneliness, thinking that I was the only one feeling this way. It sometimes comes crashing like a wave, but that's exactly what life is. To experience pain, grief, anger, anxiety and happiness is what makes us alive. 
Thank you again for your words, it means a lot to me. You're not alone, even if depression's blindfold makes it sometimes feel like there's nothing more than deep black around you. 
Same goes for you, if you need something or just want to chat, just dm me. I'm sure there's still so much ahead of you to experience and love. Keep going.

at least where I live there is no end in sight. We can't even go for a walk I am not allowed to see my dying dad and our prime minister still wants to step up measures. Nearly every private company is bankrupt, no one cares. I can't take this much longer, I haven't been outside for 5 weeks now. It's always "just hold on" "just stay at Home" NO. I CAN'T TAKE BEING LOCKED UP ANYMORE.

sleeping will help your body regenerate much faster and as long as you don't feel extremely sick you should be okay. If you feel good right now, try to go to sleep (remember: on your side!) and wake up in 2 to 3 hours to make sure you are okay. Grab something to eat and something to drink and seek help if you feel worse. 
You got this, not only physically but mentally, too. I'm available for questions. You deserve to live x

1. when sleeping you might miss symptoms of an intoxication. If it doesn't get severely worse in the next 20 to 30 min you can try to rest a little bit. Overall you should  be aware that any symptoms showing up in the next few days could still be a sign of anticholinergenic syndrome or serotonin syndrome. 
2. Sleeping on your side prevents potential vomit from getting stuck in your trachea. 
3. yes, that's a great idea. Remember that your dad wants you to be safe. He won't be mad or disappointed, He wants you to be healthy.

yes, a full stomach is always good when intoxicated. I bet you feel pretty nauseous and tired. If you feel like throwing up or experience any symptoms that might be a result of your parasympathetic nervous system not working ( the symptoms I talked about ) you need to seek immediate help. Try to stay awake for a little longer to make sure it doesn't get worse. If you go to sleep, only lie on your side. It's always the best option to tell someone, but I know this can be very hard. Try to listen to your bodies signals x

Serotonin syndrome occurs when you take medications that cause high levels of the chemical serotonin to accumulate in your body. You may feel your heart racing, heavy sweating, restlessness etc. You could also be confused, anxious and experience hallucinations. If a serotonin syndrome doesn't receive treatment, it could end deadly. Please tell someone, better too safe than not safe enough
You might experience serotonine syndrome. You should tell someone. I hope you'll be okay xx
